slides.title: Febrile Seizures: Simple vs Complex
slides.subtitle: High-yield NEET-PG & INI-CET revision in 9 slides

slides.title: Definition & Core Criteria
slides.subtitle: AAP & Nelson criteria
points: Age: **6 to 60 months** (5 yrs), with peak at **12–18 months**
Fever **≥ 38°C (100.4°F)** by any measurement method
No **CNS infection**, metabolic cause, or prior afebrile seizure
Affects **2–5%** of all neurologically healthy children
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Fever may be noticed AFTER the seizure; still counts!

slides.title: Simple vs Complex Febrile Seizure
slides.subtitle: Simple (80–85%) || Complex (15–20%)
points: Duration **< 15 minutes** || Duration **≥ 15 minutes**
**Generalized** (usually GTCS) || **Focal** onset or features
**Single** episode in 24 hrs || **≥ 2 episodes** in 24 hrs
No focal deficits || **Todd's paresis** may occur
slides.highlight: Red flag: Seizure ≥ 30 min = Febrile Status Epilepticus.

slides.title: Lumbar Puncture & Workup
slides.subtitle: AAP & IAP guidelines
points: LP **strongly indicated** if **meningism** or CNS infection suspected
Consider LP in **6–12 mo** if unimmunized (Hib/PCV) per AAP
Consider LP if **prior antibiotics** may mask meningitis
**Routine EEG / CT / MRI** NOT indicated in simple FS
Routine **blood labs** not needed unless clinically indicated
slides.highlight: PYQ: Routine neuroimaging has NO role in simple febrile seizures.

slides.title: Acute Management Protocol
slides.subtitle: Stabilize first
points: **ABC** & lateral position; most stop **spontaneously < 5 min**
If **> 5 min**: **Midazolam** 0.2 mg/kg IN/buccal or 0.1–0.2 mg/kg IV stat
Or **Lorazepam** 0.1 mg/kg IV / **Diazepam** 0.5 mg/kg PR stat
**Paracetamol** 15 mg/kg/dose PO q6h for **comfort only**
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Antipyretics DO NOT prevent seizure recurrence!

slides.title: Recurrence & Epilepsy Risk
slides.subtitle: Prognosis numbers to remember
points: Recurrence: **~30%** overall (**50%** if age < 1 yr at 1st FS)
Predictors: **Age < 1 yr**, **family H/O** FS, **low-grade** fever
Short **fever duration (< 24 hr)** before seizure raises risk
Epilepsy risk: **1–2%** in simple vs **4–6%** in complex FS
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Simple FS does NOT cause intellectual disability.

slides.title: Prophylaxis: AAP vs IAP
slides.subtitle: Preventive therapy rules
points: Continuous AEDs **NOT recommended** for simple FS (AAP & IAP)
Intermittent (**IAP**): **Clobazam** 0.75–1 mg/kg/day PO BD x 2–3d
Alternative: **Diazepam** 0.33 mg/kg/dose PO q8h during fever
IAP considers it in **frequent recurrences** or **remote access**
Core step: **Parental counseling** & **recovery position** demo
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Phenytoin & carbamazepine are INEFFECTIVE in FS.

slides.title: High-Yield Exam Takeaways
slides.subtitle: Last-minute revision
points: Simple = **< 15 min**, **generalized**, **1 episode** in 24h
**No routine EEG/MRI/labs** in simple febrile seizures
**Antipyretics** improve comfort, **do not prevent** recurrence
Age **< 1 year** is the strongest predictor of **recurrence**
slides.highlight: Peak age: 12–18 months | Simple FS prognosis: Excellent!

caption:
Simple vs Complex Febrile Seizures — one of the highest-yield peds PYQs! ⚡

Here is everything you need to ace ward rounds & NEET-PG/INI-CET:
• Exact age, fever & duration cut-offs
• When to actually tap (LP) & when to skip CT/EEG
• Acute benzodiazepine doses & IAP clobazam prophylaxis

Quick PYQ check: A 10-month-old has 2 brief generalized seizures with fever in 12 hours — simple or complex? Drop your answer below! 👇

Save 🔖 & share with a batchmate

For education only; follow local protocols.
references: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics (Chapter on Febrile Seizures)
American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) Clinical Practice Guideline: Neurodiagnostic Evaluation of Simple Febrile Seizures (2011) & Long-term Management (2008)
Indian Academy of Pediatrics (IAP) Standard Treatment Guidelines: Febrile Seizures (2022)
doctor_check: Slides 2 & 8: Updated peak incidence age from 14–18 months to 12–18 months to align with current Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics.
Slide 4: Changed 'LP mandatory' to 'LP strongly indicated' so contraindications like raised ICP or cardiorespiratory instability are not overlooked.

Slide 5: Added 'stat' frequency to acute benzodiazepine rescue doses (Midazolam, Lorazepam, Diazepam); note that institutional max single-dose caps (e.g., Lorazepam max 4 mg, Midazolam max 10 mg) apply.
Slide 6: Changed 'fever-to-seizure interval (< 1 hr)' to 'fever duration (< 24 hr) before seizure' to match Nelson's major recurrence risk factor criteria.

Slide 7: Added explicit 'PO' route to oral Diazepam (0.33 mg/kg/dose PO q8h) and attributed intermittent prophylaxis indications specifically to IAP, as AAP does not recommend intermittent prophylaxis for simple febrile seizures.
